official.deadline_note: Closing dates are per commencing trimester: Trimester 3 2026 closed 15 August 2026; Trimester 1 2027 closes 28 November 2026 (2 January 2027 for students completing Australian Year 12); Trimester 2 2027 closes 10 April 2027.
official.application_cycle: Trimester 1 2027 intake (next open round); outcomes for T1 2027 advised by 11 December 2026
official.status_note: The page publishes the 28 November 2026 closing date for students commencing Trimester 1 2027 and the 10 April 2027 date for Trimester 2 2027, so the next round is open.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award value is published as '50% of tuition fees' and 'Scholarship applies to undergraduate or postgraduate coursework tuition fees only'.
benefits: Valid for your whole degree, subject to meeting ongoing eligibility requirements
eligibility: Be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand
Be a new, commencing student who has received an offer to study by the scholarship application closing date
Have a minimum GPA in previous studies of 6.0 or above on a 7 point scale or equivalent
Satisfy all academic and English language entry requirements for your chosen undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program
Be a full-time student starting in 2026 or 2027
requirements: Students must be International Fee Paying to qualify for the scholarship and each scholarship deduction; any change from International Fee Paying status ends the scholarship
Students must be enrolled full-time, making progress in their studies and meeting their student visa requirements, unless credit prevents full-time enrolment
Students must pass all courses each trimester and progress to enrol in the next, and maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 point grading scale
Students must remain enrolled in the program named in the Letter of Offer issued by Griffith International Admissions
Deferral of scholarships is not permitted
Recipients are expected to be profiled in marketing activities for Griffith University
documents: Certified or attested true copies of educational certificates and academic transcripts demonstrating strong academic merit
Personal statement of 250 to 500 words addressing why you are applying, your selected program at Griffith, and how you will use your degree to make an impact
selection_criteria: A University panel reviews the application if all eligibility requirements are met
The scholarship is competitive and scholarship numbers are limited; when the limit for acceptances is reached the scholarships are withdrawn
coverage: 50% of undergraduate or postgraduate coursework tuition fees only, for the duration of the program
Living costs, accommodation and travel are not covered
application_method: Apply to study an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework program at Griffith University
Once you have your Letter of Offer, apply for the scholarship by the closing date for your commencing trimester
Attach academic records and a personal statement to the scholarship application
A University panel reviews the application if you meet all the eligibility requirements
Accept both your program offer and the scholarship by the deadline in your Scholarship Letter
official.application_route: Apply to study first, receive a Letter of Offer, then submit the separate Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship form by the trimester closing date.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicant must be a citizen of a country other than Australia or New Zealand.
official.international_eligibility: Open to international students only; Australian and New Zealand citizens are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programs only. Excludes Higher Degree Research, online programs, non-award, Study Abroad, Diploma programs, Masters Qualifying Program, MBA (program code 5158), Griffith English Language Institute programs, part-time-only programs, and programs delivered onshore or offshore with a partner organisation.
official.research_requirement: Not applicable to this scholarship; Higher Degree Research programs are excluded.
official.duration: Valid for your whole degree, subject to meeting ongoing eligibility requirements
official.description: Griffith University's Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship rewards a number of exceptional international students commencing undergraduate and postgraduate coursework degree programs each year, with an award value of 50% of tuition fees.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a 50% tuition waiver, not a living scholarship, so budget for the other half of your fees plus rent, food and insurance out of pocket. The scholarship cannot be applied for until you already hold a Griffith Letter of Offer, which means your application to study must be submitted well before 28 November 2026 if you are targeting Trimester 1 2027. If your grades come through a 7-point scale, the 6.0 GPA threshold is materially higher than the 4.5 threshold on Griffith's automatic merit scholarship, so check your transcript conversion before deciding which to rely on.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international applicants who already hold a Griffith offer for a full-time coursework degree and can fund half their tuition plus all living costs themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit your application to study and secure a conditional or unconditional Griffith Letter of Offer before the scholarship closing date for your intake
Have your academic certificates and transcripts formally certified or attested, not just scanned
Draft the 250 to 500 word personal statement so it names your program and your intended impact, not generic leadership language
Convert your GPA to the Griffith 7-point scale and confirm it clears 6.0, keeping the conversion evidence with your file
Diary the acceptance deadline stated in your Scholarship Letter, since failing to accept by that date withdraws the award
common_rejection_risks: Applying for the scholarship before receiving the Letter of Offer, which makes the application ineligible
Submitting an uncertified or unattested transcript, or a personal statement outside the 250 to 500 word range
Choosing an excluded program, most often the MBA (5158), a Diploma, an online or partner-delivered program, or any Higher Degree Research degree
Dropping below a 5.5 cumulative GPA or failing a course, which ends the fee deductions for later years
Late acceptance of the scholarship offer, which Griffith treats as a withdrawal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Roughly half of your tuition fees for the whole degree, plus all living costs, accommodation, overseas student health cover, flights and visa costs, none of which this scholarship funds.
document_audit: Certified or attested copies are required - plain photocopies of certificates and transcripts are the most common reason an otherwise strong application is not progressed
The personal statement must be 250 to 500 words and must reference your specific Griffith program and your intended impact
You must already hold a conditional or unconditional offer for the program named in your application
alerts: The panel only reviews your scholarship application after your offer is issued, so a slow admission decision eats into the scholarship window
Scholarship numbers are capped and the award is withdrawn once the cap is reached, so an early submission matters even within the window
Deferral is not permitted, so if you cannot start in your intended trimester you lose the scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to study at Griffith, wait for the Letter of Offer, then complete the online Vice Chancellor's International Scholarship form with certified transcripts and the personal statement before the closing date for your commencing trimester.
